result.reason: H1 most closely parallels T2 (task-continuity, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) and T5 (configuration-identity, SCOPED_CAPITAL), but the decisive difference is H1's mixed reconstruction profile. A compact semantic checkpoint whose fields are mostly reconstructable from current owner truth, with only a small subset holding participant-selected commitments or unresolved identities unavailable elsewhere, mirrors the pattern in T5: two owners need bindings but schemas differ substantially, and only one composition was demonstrated — so the value is bounded/local/option-value rather than broadly transferable. H1 lacks the strong independent-consumer evidence of T2 (durable owner state with clear lifecycle/owner consumed across replacement) or T4 (multiple owners and formal evaluation consuming the same relation semantics). Nor does H1 show the repeated-unowned-stable-responsibility trajectory of T8. The small non-reconstructable subset (commitments, unresolved identities) is preserved by current owner truth for most fields, limiting the checkpoint to a bounded local convenience — the read-only projection/export pattern seen in T4/T6 suggests a run-once exporter could serve current consumers, but no independent consumer or repeated responsibility is demonstrated for a broad transferable checkpoint authority. SCOPED_CAPITAL is the best-supported prediction: useful at a bounded owner-local scope, not demonstrated as broad transferable capital.

H1 shares the core structural signature of T1 (semantic-core-v0) and T3 (temporal-cognitive-graph): it proposes a persistent shared artifact (a checkpoint) whose content substantially duplicates truth already recoverable from existing owner-native sources—'Many checkpoint fields are also reconstructable from current owner truth.' Only a 'smaller subset' contains commitments/identifiers unavailable elsewhere. The training evidence shows that proposals externalizing shared state/authority beyond owner-native projections fail (T1=SCOPED, T3=NO_CAPITAL) unless a demonstrated independent consumer requires the shared artifact (as with T4/T7/T8, which were TRANSFERRED because multiple owners/evaluation loops actually consumed the same semantics). Here, no later independent consumer or repeated responsibility is evidenced for the checkpoint; the value is bounded to the option of resuming without rereading history, i.e., a local/potential benefit not yet demonstrated as broad transferable capital. This matches SCOPED_CAPITAL, not NO_CAPITAL, because the narrowly-held participant-selected commitments do constitute a real (if bounded) future option not fully reconstructable elsewhere, analogous to T1's bounded usefulness and unlike T3/T6 which duplicated authority entirely.

The holdout H2 describes two digest-bound scoped HTTPS CONNECT paths retained beside ambient networking. Ambient networking already completes all currently tested useful work, while the scoped paths are only materially faster on some services and preserve option value under future ambient failures. This mirrors the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern seen in T1 (semantic core externalizes many semantics but mature mechanisms already own the mechanics; useful at local/option-value scope, not demonstrated broad transferable capital) and especially T5 (digest-bound opaque identity bindings preserve option value while a second non-Evaluation owner composition was not yet demonstrated). Like T5, H2's digest-bound scoped paths have no demonstrated independent consumer requiring them today—all useful work is already handled by ambient networking. The 'materially faster on some services' and 'option value under future failures' clauses are exactly bounded/local/option-value scope, not broad transferable value. It does not match TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL (no later independent consumption or repeated responsibility demonstrated) nor NO_CAPITAL (no evidence of failure, deletion, or unpromotion; the paths are retained, paralleling SCOPED_CAPITAL outcomes). The evidence-inferred regularity: beneficial-but-not-yet-independently-consumed retained option value with a scoped benefit (some services, future failure scenarios) maps to SCOPED_CAPITAL, consistent with T1 and T5 patterns where local/limited/option-value utility without demonstrated broad independent consumption stays SCOPED.

H2 mirrors the SCOPED_CAPITAL patterns in the training evidence rather than the TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL ones. The scoped egress paths are explicitly described as materially faster 'on some services' and preserving 'option value' under future failures — both bounded/optional justifications, comparable to T5 (where a second owner composition had not yet demonstrated shared schema, limiting it to SCOPED_CAPITAL) and T4's early state (which only became TRANSFERRED after multiple owners and formal evaluation consumed the same relation semantics). H2 has no demonstrated later independent consumer or repeated responsibility: ambient networking currently completes all tested useful work, so the scoped paths serve as an availability/performance option, not a stable evidenced reuse responsibility. It also requires 'dedicated services and qualification', similar to T1's noted compatibility/authority surface costs that kept that change SCOPED. Contrast with true TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL records (T2, T4, T7): each had later independent consumption or repeated responsibility evidenced within the stated change itself (survival across replacement; multiple owners and formal evaluation consuming the same semantics; subsequent Computer self-audit consumption). H2 states only potential option value and currently unexercised performance advantages, with no demonstrated future consumer. This matches the NO_CAPITAL boundary too but does not reach it: the paths are concrete working artifacts that could be promoted later, so SCOPED_CAPITAL (option-value scope) is the best-fit label.

H3 is a model-visible prior learned from earlier Game work, applied to later rescue behavior. The evidence pattern from training labels distinguishes transferred capital by demonstrated later independent consumption or repeated responsibility at a stable evidenced scope (T2, T4, T7, T8 all have concrete later consumers or repeated applications described). H3's description only states the prior 'changes how the model reasons' about custody/responsibility and that its effect on a later multi-turn objective is indirect and depends on many subsequent policy choices. There is no demonstrated stable, independent consumer or repeated responsibility analogous to T7's Computer self-audit or T8's repeated use. The value is bounded to the specific game/rescue domain and contingent on downstream policy, matching the SCOPED_CAPITAL pattern (bounded/local/partial/option-value scope, not broad transferable capital). It is not NO_CAPITAL because it is retained and applied to later rescue behavior (a real demonstrated usage), but it lacks the stable transferred scope shown by TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL cases.

H3 is a model-visible prior from earlier Game work applied to later rescue behavior. Comparing with the training evidence, T2 (TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) and T7 (TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) both involved durable owners/authority boundaries with clear lifecycles and repeated independent consumption by formal/dedicated consumers. T8 (TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL) had a reusable structural rule with repeated unowned stable responsibility. In contrast, H3's prior changes model reasoning about custody/responsibility but its downstream effect is indirect and depends on many subsequent policy choices — so there is no demonstrated stable owner or repeated independent consumer binding the prior to later value. It resembles T5 (SCOPED_CAPITAL), where a mechanism was useful within bounded compositional contexts but lacked a second real consumer demonstrating broad transfer. The evidence only shows a bounded/contextual application (rescue behavior within Game/rescue scope) with no demonstrated broad transferable consumption, so SCOPED_CAPITAL is the best-supported label. The knowledge is domain (rescue/custody) but its generalization is not demonstrated — the indirectness and dependency on subsequent policy choices undermine evidence of stable reusable adaptive value at a broader scope.

The strongest analogues are T4 (observation-minimum) and T2 (task-continuity), both TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. T4 moved exact authoritative reconstruction out of a model into a deterministic read-only owner exporter/projection consumed by multiple owners and formal evaluation; H4 likewise moves exact repeated source-history aggregation out of model reasoning into a deterministic Security-local reducer/projection that the model consumes. The mechanism has a clear owner (Security), an exact escape hatch preserving the authoritative source, and targets a precision-sensitive arithmetic burden where manual/model-driven aggregation repeatedly costs attention — matching the signature for transferable adaptive capital. It does not duplicate truth or create a new authority surface: the projection is owner-local and the underlying source remains authoritative, distinguishing it from NO_CAPITAL failures (T3 temporal-cognitive-graph proposed a new shared graph authority with no independent consumer; T6 global-usage-authority duplicated truth). While only a single consumer (Security model consumption) is cited, the stable owner-local deterministic projection with retained source authority mirrors the T4/T2 pattern where durable owner state and read-only projections proved reusable across model/owner replacement. The model still interpreting the projection correctly is a bounded correctness risk, not evidence of non-transfer, since the deterministic projection removes the precision arithmetic burden regardless of downstream interpretation.

H4 matches the recurring pattern in the training evidence where a precision-sensitive exact computation burden is externalized from model reasoning into a deterministic owner-local reducer/projection with an exact escape hatch. This is structurally analogous to T4 (observation-minimum) and T2 (task-continuity), both rated TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL: the change localizes exact reconstruction/state into an owner-owned deterministic mechanism while the model consumes the projection, and the mechanism is consumed repeatedly by a clear recurring responsibility (comparison/evaluation in T4; request identity/continuity in T2). H4 has a clear single owner (Security), a precise 'exact arithmetic' target, and an exact escape hatch preserving the original source as authority — mirroring T4's 'owner recovery remains independent of the projection' property that supported transfer. Unlike T5 (SCOPED_CAPITAL), which lacked a second real non-Evaluation consumer and had divergent schemas, H4's reducer/projection targets a class of exact source-history aggregation within a single owner and is consumed by the same recurring arithmetic task. Unlike T1/T3/T6 (NO_CAPITAL), H4 introduces no new authority/compatibility surface or global writable database — the deterministic reducer is precisely scoped, owner-native, and read-only-projected, matching the promoted changes' defining characteristics. Under the inference rule that a stable bounded owner with a recurrent precision workload that is exact-reconstructable from authoritative history predicts transferable reusable capital, H4 is best classified as TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. The model-interpretation requirement parallels T4 where consumers must read the projection correctly and does not undercut the demonstrated reusable value.

H5 matches the TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL pattern evidenced by T2, T4, T7, and T8. H5 is a production rule (a stable reusable procedure/policy) explicitly intended for later ordinary Web/Studio production, not a one-off original page — analogous to T7 (bounded agent-led method consumed repeatedly by the experiment loop and later audit) and T8 (reusable infrastructure-promotion rule guiding heterogeneous later decisions). The evidence supporting TRANSFERRED is: (1) a clear reproducible procedure (inspect exact rendered pixels) with a direct observable artifact, analogous to T4's read-only exporter/query projection that multiple owners consume; (2) an explicit 'later ordinary Web/Studio production' intended consumption beyond the originating case, demonstrating intended repeat responsibility rather than bounded one-time scope; (3) a bounded correction path and exact unchanged controls, indicating stability across reuse like T2's durable owner state with clear lifecycle. This contrasts with NO_CAPITAL cases: T3 (temporal graph) was declined because no independent consumer required graph storage/authority, whereas H5 has an intended consumer base (Web/Studio production). It also contrasts with SCOPED_CAPITAL cases: T1 was scoped because mature mechanisms already owned the mechanics, and T5 was scoped because only one non-owner composition was demonstrated — H5 has no existing mechanism owning the pixel-inspection semantics and names a broader later consumption scope, so the intended repeated responsibility supports transfer at a stable evidenced scope.

diagnosticMessageTail.content:
You are studying which adaptive changes become useful future capital. Infer only regularities supported by visible evidence. Do not assume implementation size, recursive depth, abstraction, or persistence automatically implies later value.

OUTCOME LABELS:
NO_CAPITAL: No demonstrated reusable adaptive value; failed/unpromoted/deleted as a general change.
SCOPED_CAPITAL: Useful only at a bounded/local/partial/option-value scope; not demonstrated as broad transferable capital.
TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL: Later independent consumption or repeated responsibility demonstrates reusable adaptive value at a stable evidenced scope.

TRAINING EVIDENCE:
T1 — semantic-core-v0
CHANGE: A large experimental Agent semantic kernel externalizes identity, state, effect and conformance into one shared reference implementation. Live dogfood shows the prototype can express many desired semantics, but mature operating systems/databases/workflow mechanisms already own much of the mechanics and a shared kernel would become a new authority/compatibility surface.

T2 — task-continuity
CHANGE: Open semantic work and unresolved external request identity must survive model, Provider, process and Session replacement. Transcript/session-only baselines cannot reliably recover private commitments or unknown external effects after replacement; durable owner state has a clear lifecycle and owner.

T3 — temporal-cognitive-graph
CHANGE: A proposed temporal cognitive graph externalizes support, contradiction, dependency and supersession relations because chronological transcripts are awkward. Simpler current-source retrieval and typed working-state baselines have not yet failed, and no materially independent consumer requires graph storage or graph authority.

T4 — observation-minimum
CHANGE: Host, Harness and Runtime retain independent authoritative histories, but cross-owner evaluation repeatedly pays manual joining cost. Run-once read-only owner exporters plus a rebuildable selection/query projection reconstruct exact trajectories while owner recovery remains independent of the projection. Multiple owners and formal evaluation consume the same relation semantics.

T5 — configuration-identity
CHANGE: Evaluation and Security both need to bind material environment/configuration identity, but their payload schemas differ substantially. A Computing composition experiment can preserve each owner record as an opaque immutable binding and compare digests without copying domain fields; a second real non-Evaluation owner composition has not yet demonstrated a shared schema.

T6 — global-usage-authority
CHANGE: Harness owns model/Run usage, Runtime owns physical execution measurements and domains own domain costs. Cross-run comparisons need some normalized numbers, but owner-native measurements can be projected read-only and the numeric fields have different semantics and authority. A global writable usage database would duplicate truth.

T7 — agent-first-research-method
CHANGE: Research repeatedly spends human attention selecting routine next experiments, reconstructing burdens and deciding whether to retain candidate structures. A bounded Agent-led method with frozen oracle, authority boundary, falsifier, deletion and rollback is consumed by the experiment loop and later by Computer self-audit while product/domain promotion stays owner-controlled.

T8 — infrastructure-promotion-rule
CHANGE: Cross-project usefulness repeatedly tempts new shared services. A reusable rule says to inherit mature mechanisms first, then add the smallest owner-local projection, and promote a shared semantic boundary only after repeated unowned stable responsibility; repository/service extraction is a separate later gate. The rule is intended to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions.

DELAYED OUTCOME RECORDS, BOUND BY STABLE ID:
T1 = SCOPED_CAPITAL
T2 = TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL
T3 = NO_CAPITAL
T4 = TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL
T5 = SCOPED_CAPITAL
T6 = NO_CAPITAL
T7 = TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL
T8 = TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL

HOLDOUT CHANGE:
H5 — render-review-prior
Retain the production rule that when expression/layout matters, inspect exact rendered pixels rather than treating source/build/browser mechanics as semantic proof. The procedure has a direct observable artifact, a bounded correction path and exact unchanged controls; it is intended for later ordinary Web/Studio production rather than one original page.

TASK:
Predict this change’s later adaptive-capital outcome.

Return selectedOperation EXACTLY as one of NO_CAPITAL, SCOPED_CAPITAL, TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. Set owner to Ordivon Computing, needsMoreInfo=false, effectClass=read_only, authorityBoundary=Computing research only. Explain the prediction in reason.

result.reason: H6 matches the pattern of demonstrated transferred capital changes (T2, T4, T7, T8) rather than SCOPED or NO_CAPITAL ones. T2/T4/T7 evidence shows transferred capital requires a stable owner lifecycle with repeated independent consumers addressing the same recurring need, where native evidence remains authoritative and the change is a minimal read-only projection rather than a new authority. H6's 'fresh Agents repeatedly reconstruct route affordances from raw configuration' demonstrates repeated independent consumption addressing the same semantic need; the narrow read-only projection with native evidence reachable and no central registry mirrors T4's read-only owner exporters with owner recovery independent of projection, and T7's bounded agent-side surface that leaves authority owner-controlled. This is not T1/T5-style SCOPED_CAPITAL (a broad shared kernel/schema authority with no second consumers) nor T3/T6-style NO_CAPITAL (a proposed surface with no demonstrated consumer pressure or a global writable authority). H6 has demonstrated repeated consumer demand (repeated reconstruction) and avoids creating new authority/compatibility surface (leaves route selection and effects to Agent, no central registry), satisfying the transferred-capital criterion of later independent repeated responsibility at a stable evidenced scope. The change is read-only (effectClass), confined to Computing research (authorityBoundary), and the repeated reconstruction demonstrates stable recurring responsibility. Predicting NO_CAPITAL would ignore the demonstrated repeated consumption, and predicting SCOPED_CAPITAL would understate the stable, repeatable consumer evidence analogous to T2/T4/T7/T8.

H6 mirrors the pattern in TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL cases T4 and T7, and the NO_CAPITAL cases T3/T6 are distinguished by absence of demonstrated cross-owner consumption. The training evidence shows that transformations from an owner-native representation into a read-only normalized projection succeed when repeated consumption exists. T4 (observation-minimum) was promoted because 'multiple owners and formal evaluation consume the same relation semantics' — repeated consumers paying a joining cost justified the projection, while owners retained independent authority. T7 was promoted because the bounded method was consumed by the experiment loop and later by Computer self-audit. H6 states 'fresh Agents repeatedly reconstruct route affordances from raw configuration' — that is an established repeated, cross-Agent consumption burden, satisfying the repeated-independent-consumption condition. Like T4 and T7, H6 explicitly leaves native evidence reachable and effects/authority with the owner ('leaves route selection and all effects to the Agent, keeps native evidence reachable'), matching the read-only projection principle rather than a new authority. The absence of a central capability registry avoids the T3 failure mode (graph authority with no independent consumer) and the T6 failure mode (global writable duplicate truth). The repeated reconstruction pain is concretely demonstrated ('fresh Agents repeatedly'), unlike T3 where 'no materially independent consumer requires' the new storage and simpler baselines had 'not yet failed,' and unlike T5 where only one real non-Evaluation consumer existed (SCOPED). The comparison is SCOPED vs TRANSFERRED; H6 has repeated cross-Agent consumption of the same relation (route affordances), analogous to T4's multiple owners and T7's multiple consumers, so TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL is the best-supported label.

H7 carries the Infrastructure Promotion Rule (T8) into later heterogeneous architecture/owner decisions as a fixed prompt prior. The rule itself is a general heuristic, but the evidence supports only a bounded scope: the holdout says it adds no new owner facts and may bias different model families differently, with value conditional on whether the historical rule generalizes. T8 was TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL, which is the closest template. However, H7 differs materially from T8 in key respects: (a) it is applied as a fixed static prior rather than an active decision procedure, so it no longer has the repeated unowned stable responsibility test or the promotion gate actively exercised; (b) it may bias model families differently, creating heterogeneous/uneven effects rather than stable reusable value; (c) the claim that it reduces architecture over-promotion is explicitly conditional ('if the historical rule generalizes'), so no later independent consumption or repeated responsibility is demonstrated by the provided evidence. Comparing to T5 (SCOPED_CAPITAL), which also involved a promising schema/composition principle that was not yet independently consumed across owners, H7's value remains at option/local scope: it may help when the rule happens to match a given architecture decision, but the evidence does not show stable transferable consumption across heterogeneous decisions. NO_CAPITAL is too strong since the rule has demonstrated prior utility in T8 and may carry forward; TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL requires demonstrated later independent consumption or repeated responsibility, which the holdout only conditions on rather than evidences. Therefore SCOPED_CAPITAL best matches the visible evidence: bounded, conditional, option-value applicability rather than demonstrated broad transferable capital.

H7 carries the Infrastructure Promotion Rule (T8) forward as a fixed prompt prior for a later heterogeneous set of architecture/owner decisions. T8 itself was TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL: it was an explicit reusable rule already demonstrated to guide heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions and was kept as a stable rule rather than deleted. H7 directly operationalizes that transfer by injecting the same rule into a later, differently-scoped set of decisions, i.e., repeated responsibility consuming the rule as reusable adaptive value. The training evidence pattern (T8 and T7 both transferred because they were stable, owner-controlled rules/methods later consumed independently) supports that an already-transferred capital rule carried to a new but analogous domain retains its transferable value. Unlike T3 and T6 (which lacked independent consumers or duplicated owner truth) and unlike T1/T5 (scoped to a single authority surface), H7's change is the application of an already-proven general rule—not a new authority claim or a new shared ownership surface—and therefore the stable, repeatedly-consumed rule scope is evidenced. The modest risk that different model families bias differently does not contradict transfer: the historical rule already generalizes across heterogeneous decisions, and the prior adds no owner facts that could create authority conflicts, so broad reusable value at a stable scope is the supported prediction.

H8 most closely parallels T7 (agent-first-research-method), which was TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. Both are procedure/method changes that replace repeated human attention with a bounded, repeatable decision procedure, and both are applied across heterogeneous domains (T7 across experiment loop and Computer self-audit; H8 across a different materially distinct professional-equipment decision family). T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule) also supports this: a reusable rule intended to guide heterogeneous later decisions became TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL, and H8 is a generalization of exactly that kind of cross-domain disposition/promotion guidance. The explicit evidence of applying the same checklist to a materially different decision family demonstrates the pattern of repeated independent consumption across distinct domains that the TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL label requires, versus SCOPED_CAPITAL where utility remains at bounded/local scope and NO_CAPITAL where no demonstrated positive adaptive value exists. The changed scope (generic rather than static prior) is not merely a local option; it is consumed again in an unrelated professional-equipment family, evidencing stable reusable value at a demonstrable scope.

The pattern in T7 and T8 establishes that reusable decision/calibration procedures become TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL when they are consumed repeatedly across materially different contexts with owner-controlled authority boundaries. T7 (agent-first-research-method) was a bounded Agent-led method (frozen oracle, authority boundary, falsifier, deletion, rollback) consumed by both the experiment loop and later Computer self-audit, and was TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. T8 (infrastructure-promotion-rule) was a reusable rule guiding heterogeneous later infrastructure decisions and was TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL. H8 (generic-calibration-checklist) matches both: it is a reusable procedure applied to the current change's disposition choice AND explicitly applied to a materially different professional-equipment decision family, demonstrating cross-domain transfer. Its enumerated operational dimensions (current consumer, incremental outcome, simpler baseline, recurring cost/coupling, authority fit, reopen/deletion) mirror T7/T8's explicit authority-boundary and deletion/rollback mechanics, and the 'reopen/deletion' item preserves an open owner-controlled gate rather than creating new authority. Unlike T3 (proposed temporal graph with no independent consumer) or T6 (duplicate truth), H8 introduces no new authority surface or duplicated truth; it externalizes an evaluation procedure that is consumed by multiple decision families within owner-controlled scope. No T1/T5-style shared-schema/authority conflict appears because the checklist is generic procedure, not a new persistent shared kernel or record format. The repeated consumption across a second unrelated decision family demonstrates transferable adaptive value at a stable evidenced scope, matching the TRANSFERRED_CAPITAL threshold.
